questions.prompt: Which customer description is the most specific?

choices.text: Small businesses of every kind everywhere in the whole world
Anyone in Texas who might want to buy things

questions.correct_answer: Owners of food trucks in Austin who take card payments
questions.intro: "Everyone" is not a customer. A specific customer is a group you can describe and find: who they are, what situation they are in, and where they can be reached. "Busy people" is too broad. "Parents of children ages 6 to 10 who both work full time in our town" is specific. A specific customer helps you choose words, prices, and places to advertise. You can widen the group later, after you learn what works for the first group.
questions.feedback: A specific type of owner, place and situation makes a group you can find.

questions.prompt: Which step narrows "people who need meals" by situation?

choices.text: People who eat food
People recovering from surgery
People who live on planet Earth
People who like meals

questions.intro: Narrowing works in steps. Start with "people who need meals." Add a situation: "people who need meals after surgery." Add a place: "in our city." Add who decides: "usually a family member who orders." Each step removes people who are unlikely to buy and keeps the ones with a clear need. A narrow group is not small thinking; it is a clear target you can actually reach and serve well.
questions.feedback: A situation like surgery recovery narrows the group.
